candidates.memorySpeedTradeoff: Provider partition copies or implicit precision changes may erase acceleration or fail correctness. Startup/compiled caches and shared resident weights need separate measurements.

candidates.hypothesis: Safe eval-mode Conv->BatchNorm folding may remove passes and activation traffic in IR-SE residual and shortcut paths.
candidates.control: Unmodified deployed eval graph with fixed running statistics and FP32 output.
candidates.proposedChange: Fold only mathematically valid Conv->BN sequences, including input/shortcut/end-residual locations, before export. Do not fold a leading BN across a padded convolution or across PReLU/SE nonlinearities. Hash each transformed graph and check per-block outputs before full e4e.
candidates.memorySpeedTradeoff: Removes intermediate traffic and dispatches with little extra residency, but changes floating-point operation ordering and may fail the unchanged W+ gate.

candidates.hypothesis: Independent same-resolution style heads may benefit from grouped dispatch while retaining all distinct learned weights.

candidates.memorySpeedTradeoff: Parallel heads expand activations and live weights; compare groups and stop when memory pressure outweighs dispatch savings. No weight sharing or fine-head omission is allowed.

candidates.hypothesis: CPU encoding plus an independently validated GPU synthesis route may deliver a useful photo workflow before GPU e4e is qualified on that device.

candidates.memorySpeedTradeoff: Only36KiB W+ crosses the boundary, but encoder and generator runtimes can duplicate memory; combine with measured phase residency rather than assuming overlap is best.

candidates.hypothesis: Repeat uploads can avoid alignment/e4e work when exact photo/preprocessing/model identities match; this is reuse, not an inference speedup.

candidates.memorySpeedTradeoff: Stores small W+ outputs and optional originals but cache hit rates are workload-specific. Do not rank repeated-cache hits against uncached encoder timing.

candidates.hypothesis: Selective lower-precision storage or execution could reduce encoder transfer/residency, but may fail the current tight reconstruction gates.
